## Recommendation: contact **American University Washington College of Law first** — if public-interest/public-service work is genuinely your intended path

It has the clearest potential funding upside: the **PIPS Scholarship is three years of full tuition**. The outreach/application step is not as frictionless as Maryland’s information-request form or UBalt’s appointment booking, but the potential value is substantial enough to act on promptly. Its scholarship deadline is **January 31, 2027, at 11:59 PM EST**, and AUWCL says that deadline is earlier than its priority deadline for general admission.

### 1) American University Washington College of Law — first action
**Why first:** PIPS is expressly for prospective public-interest/public-service lawyers and provides full tuition for three years. AUWCL describes it as financial and programmatic support for students with strong credentials and the intention/potential to pursue a meaningful public-interest or public-service career after graduation.

**Do this next:** Start the PIPS application:  
https://american.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6FMJcuOCtqeRJiu

The application page asks for your **LSAC number and email address** to begin. AUWCL says both the electronic JD admissions application and the electronic PIPS application must be complete by the deadline. The PIPS application includes three short essays; a recommendation letter is optional but strongly recommended. AUWCL says admitted full-time JD PIPS applicants go to the PIPS selection committee, with awards beginning in March through mid-April. Its general contact number shown on the scholarship materials is **(202) 885-1000**.

**Page retained:** the dedicated PIPS Scholarship page is open in a separate tab (tab 24). I also retained AUWCL’s application/selection-details page (tab 22).

### 2) Maryland Carey Law — lowest-friction admissions outreach
**Actual mechanism to request materials:** use its **Request Information** link for the relevant program—**JD Applicants**, **LLM Applicants**, or **MS in Law Applicants**—on its Contact Admissions page, rather than merely emailing a generic address.

**Do this next:** Open the Contact Admissions page and choose **“JD Applicants”** (assuming you are pursuing a JD) under “Request Information”:  
https://www.law.umaryland.edu/admissions--aid/contact-admissions/

For a direct follow-up, the Office of Admissions lists **admissions@law.umaryland.edu**, **(410) 706-3492**, and hours of **Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM**.

**Forthcoming virtual admissions event:** **JD Info Session & Application Overview**, **Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 12:00–1:00 PM**. The school’s JD Webinar page labels it with a “Register here” link. A good practical move is to submit the request-information form first, then register and bring 2–3 targeted questions on scholarship process, public-interest pathways, and application timing.

**Page retained:** the Maryland Carey **JD Webinars** event page is open in a separate tab (tab 15); the admissions contact/request-information page is also open (tab 23).

### 3) University of Baltimore School of Law — easiest live admissions conversation
**Concrete procedure:** schedule a **30-minute phone or Zoom appointment with an admissions counselor** through the **“Schedule a 30-Minute Phone Call”** link on UBalt Law’s Visit page. UBalt characterizes it as an in-depth discussion for advice and questions not available on the website.

**Do this next:** use that booking link on:  
https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/visit/

If you prefer to arrange it directly, contact **lawadmissions@ubalt.edu** or **410-837-4459** during **8:30 AM–4:30 PM** business hours. The same page also offers an in-person tour that can be paired with an individual admissions-counselor meeting.

A separate option on that page is UBalt’s **Fall Virtual Open House**, **Tuesday, October 27, 2026, 6:00–7:00 PM ET**, via Zoom; it says no registration is required and lists password **UBaltLaw**.

**Page retained:** UBalt Law’s actual Visit/meeting-details page is open in a separate tab (tab 16).

## Practical order if you want to work all three today
1. **AUWCL:** begin the PIPS form with LSAC number/email and calendar the January 31 deadline; this preserves the strongest identified tuition opportunity.
2. **Maryland Carey:** submit the program-specific request-information form, then register for the October 14 virtual JD session.
3. **UBalt:** book the 30-minute admissions phone/Zoom slot; it is the most direct way to get customized answers quickly.

This ordering prioritizes AUWCL’s unusually concrete funding possibility while still using Maryland Carey and UBalt’s very low-effort outreach channels immediately afterward.
